context: Request: which restructuring matters involved DIP financing in any capacity (debtor, DIP lender, or creditor responding to a DIP). Rubric: 1006-00002 (Crestline), 1020-00002 (Greenfield Ag), 1024-00001 (Driftwood / Cascabel), 1011-00002 (Meridian Consumer), 1044-00003 (Thalassa, standby DIP planning), plus a precision criterion. T0 also asserted 1007-00002 (Meridian Precision Components; the firm acted for a stalking-horse buyer in a DIP-funded sale).

first_error.why: Evidence seen at [32]-[42] showed the firm acting for a stalking-horse buyer in that case, but the answer counts the matter as a DIP financing role alongside debtor, lender and creditor roles.
first_error.critic_note: (generic flag) the write review at [76] raised 'possible over-inclusion' about draft versus executed status, without naming this matter; the check stages kept it.

divergence: All three runs followed the same route: store listing, folder count, a store-wide extraction scan that surfaced all five qualifying matters, then listing and reading the main candidates' engagement letters and filings; T1 added a per-matter file-name triage and T2 a batched rescan. They split at what was read and counted: T0 also opened a matter where the firm acted for a buyer in a sale funded by the requested financing (its first reading stage) and counted it at the write stage (over-inclusion); T1 and T2 never opened that matter and limited the answer to the three roles the request names. The reviews did not differ in a way that mattered: every write-stage review raised generic over- and under-inclusion risks, and none named the extra matter in T0.
